Clear Screen Now - choosing this option will immediately clear the main screen. \n\nClear Screen with WSJT-X - Enables clearing the main screen when WSJT-X clears both panels.

If you enable this feature then the app screen will clear whenever you clear the WSJT-X screen on your computer. 

Please note: 

1) The app screen will clear when you clear both WSJT-X panels. In other words you have to double-click the WSJT-X Erase button. 

2) It may take a couple of seconds for the app screen to clear. WSJT-X does not always send the clear message immediately.

This display shows all the data from the main display plus all the background messages sent by WSJT-X or JTDX. 

Background messages are in dull white. Other messages are either green (CQ), red (your callsign), or bright white (all else). 

The display scrolls up/down/left/right. After scrolling the screen will not update for 10 seconds. A quick tap will restore updates.

This application is WiFi only. 

Please connect this device to your home WiFi. The computer running WSJT-X or JTDX must be on the same home network. 

For details visit this webpage. 

If you believe WiFi is connected please verify (via Settings) that your phone has an IP address. Some phones slip in and out of WiFi. For assistance Email feedback@feotec.com. 

Please restart this application after connecting to WiFi.
Port values can range between 1024 and 32767.\n\nIt must match the port specified in WSJT-X (or JTDX). Click Help for details.
Port values must be between 1024 and 32767 inclusive.
This application must be restarted in order for the change to take effect.

The port number is simply a number which identifies this phone app. 

You can choose any number between 1024 and 32767. However, WSJT-X (or JTDX) must be told what this port number is. This is done in the Reporting tab of the Settings window. (Detailed instructions on configuring WSJT-X are in the "Setup WSJT-X or JTDX" option of this Settings menu). 

The important point is that the number in WSJT-X (or JTDX) Settings must match the number in this application. The default for both is 2237. So if you haven't changed them then they should already match.

Filters will allow you to specify continents, countries, and callsigns that you wish to display or not display. 

Include Filters will show only the countries/continents/callsigns that you specify 

Exclude Filters will show everything except the countries/continents/callsigns that you specify. 

Reuse Previous Filters - To save time you can reuse one of your ten most recent filters. 

Edit Previous Filters - Recall and make changes to one of your ten most recent filters. 

For details see this webpage.
Choose How to Filter\n" "(select one or more)

Here you define your Include or Exclude filter. 

List of Continents or Countries - You'll choose from a list of continents or countries. Multiple selections are allowed. 

Prefix or Callsign - You'll type in the prefix you want included or excluded. For example, if you type in a three character prefix, such as VK9, then it will be compared against the first three characters of each sending station. Complete callsigns can be typed in, if desired. 

For details see this webpage.

This window displays descriptions of your previous filters (up to ten). If you use the same filter frequently then you can save time by selecting it from the list. 

The list can scroll up and down if necessary. 

The most recent filter is always the first one in the list.

This window allows you to filter on one or more of the six continents. 

For each received message the continent is determined from the sending station's callsign, using the ARRL Countries List. 

Press the OK button when complete. 

Press CLEAR-RETURN to delete all entries and return to the previous menu.

This window lists 30 major countries and allows you to filter on one or more. The display scrolls up and down. 

For each received message the country is determined from the sending station's callsign, based on the ARRL Countries List. 

Press the OK button when complete. 

Press CLEAR-RETURN to delete all entries and return to the previous menu.

This window lists all the countries in the ARRL Countries List and allows you to filter on one or more. The display scrolls up and down. 

For each received message the country is determined from the sending station's callsign, based on the ARRL Countries List. 

Press the OK button when complete. 

Press CLEAR-RETURN to delete all entries and return to the previous menu.
Enter as many Prefixes as desired.\nPress Done (on keyboard)\n" "after each entry
Enter as many Prefixes as desired.\nPress Done (on keyboard) after each entry.\nUncheck to remove prefix.

This allows you to filter on specific callsigns or the prefix of those callsigns. 

The callsign of the sending station is extracted from each message. The first few characters of that callsign are compared against what you type in here. 

You can enter multiple prefixes. Press DONE on the keyboard after each one. 

After entering a prefix it will be listed in this window. You can remove that prefix by clearing the checkbox next to it. 

Press OK when complete. Press CLEAR-RETURN to delete all entries. Both buttons will return you to the previous menu. 

For details and examples see this webpage.

My Callsign - With this option you'll be alerted when someone calls you. 

All Stations - Select this option and you'll get an alert on every station. This can be used, for example, to see if 6 meters is open. If selected then all other options are deselected.

Here you customize your alert. For more info see this webpage. 

Sound-Vibrate - Press the CHANGE button to cycle through available sound and vibration options. 

Minimum Signal - Press CHANGE and another window will appear. A station must be above this signal level before an Alert will occur. 

&rememberTitle; - Once a station causes an alert then it will not cause an alert again. 

Test Sound and Vibration - Press the TEST button and the app will attempt to beep and vibrate. 

Press the FINISH button when complete. Press CANCEL to quit.

This window displays a wheel to allow you to select the minimum signal level. 

Swipe up where it says "No Minimum" to change the setting. 

A station will not cause an alert unless it is above this signal level. 

Press the OK button when complete. 

Press CLEAR-RETURN to restore previous setting and return to the previous menu.

Possible reasons for no sound: 

1) If the ringer is silenced it usually silences notifications also. 

2) "Do Not Disturb" mode is on. 

3) The notification sound is turned down. The notification volume control is often separate from ringer or media volume. 

4) In Android Settings, this app's notifications have been silenced. 

Regarding vibration, some devices do not have a vibrator. If yours does not then this app will only give you the option of sound or silence. 

Recent Android versions have given users more control over notification sounds. For a more thorough discussion please see this webpage.

Choose What to Sort On\n" "(select one)

Each burst of stations can be sorted on one of these four parameters. 

Signal Strength - (SNR) sorted from the strongest to weakest signal. 

Frequency - sorted across the audio passband, from the lowest to highest. 

Distance - sorted from the closest to the most distance. 

Direction (Azimuth) - sorted from 0 degrees to 359 degrees. 

Sorting on distance and azimuth is done based on the station's grid square. Stations that have not provided a grid square will be listed first.

WSJT-X will make three passes to decode each FT8/FT4 burst. 

The app screen will be updated with each pass. Most stations will appear in the first update. 

Please note that each update will be sorted separately.

This display will draw lines from your grid to the grid of the most recently heard stations. 

However, your grid is unknown. 

Either WSJT-X has not sent your grid yet or it is not set in WSJT-X configuration.
There are currently no received stations that have sent their grid squares.

This display draws a line from your grid square to the grid square of the last 30 stations received. 

Only stations reporting a grid square are mapped. 

The app continues to collect data while this screen is active. 

Google Maps will not draw the entire earth. So it may be necessary to scroll the map to see everything. 

Filters – if you filter out stations they will not be mapped. However, when you turn on filtering the stations that are already mapped will not be removed until they are no longer among the last 30 stations.
Google Maps must be installed for mapping to work. \n\nThis Android device reports that Google Maps is either not installed or installed but disabled.

IMPORTANT: you have to configure WSJT-X to receive messages. Otherwise this feature won\'t work. Press the SETUP button below for instructions. \n\nFor more info see this webpage.

Do a long press (more than one second) on the Reply icon at the top of the screen (and illustrated to the right) for information and setup instructions.
